Question: Henry the donkey has a very long piece of pasta. He takes a number of bites of pasta, each time eating \(3\) inches of pasta from the middle of one piece. In the end, he has \(10\) pieces of pasta whose total length is \(17\) inches. How long, in inches, was the piece of pasta he started with?
Solution:
Each bite removes the middle of one piece and leaves two pieces in its place. Thus each bite increases the number of pieces by exactly \(1\).

Starting with \(1\) piece and finishing with \(10\) pieces requires \(10-1=9\) bites. Henry ate \(9\cdot3=27\) inches of pasta.

The original length was the amount eaten plus the amount left:

\[
27+17=\boxed{44}\text{ inches},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\). Counting how a single bite changes the number of pieces avoids confusing \(10\) final pieces with \(10\) bites.
